name: A11Y: qa6: corkboard: the “New note” tile is not a child of the card list (a listbox owns only options: its button is “list with 5 items” to a screen reader, and may be skipped in browse mode)
why: Left open: the “New note” tile sits inside the listbox of cards. Moving it out needs a wrapper that every card selector and the grid layout pass through; too much risk for a fix round.

name: UX: qa6 menus: Ungroup leaves the folder behind as an empty stack (a writer asks for it to go away)
why: A decision for the maintainer: “the folder stays” is the documented behavior (docs/plan.md). To change it: trash the folder when nothing is left in it, and teach Undo to bring it back.

name: qa6 store: UX: a comment in the binder note’s properties survives a move
why: A documented limitation (docs/file-format.md): a property write goes through Obsidian’s serializer, which rewrites the whole block and drops comments. Obsidian’s own Properties view does the same.

name: qa6 store: UX: longform: a comment in the index note’s properties survives a reorder
why: The same documented limitation: Obsidian’s serializer drops comments in the properties block.

name: BUG: qa6 writing: setting a status in a note whose properties are hand written (comments, flow lists, quotes, block text, dates, CRLF) changes only the status line
why: The same documented limitation: Obsidian’s serializer rewrites the whole properties block (comments dropped, flow lists and quoting normalised). The note’s text is untouched.

name: PERF: qa6 phone: a flat binder of 1,000 short scenes, CPU four times slower: every mode opens in under 2 s, and swiping through the manuscript is as smooth as through the board (95 of 100 frames under 50 ms)
why: Left open: swiping fast through 1,000 scenes hitches as each section becomes its editor (the cost of creating one editor, which can’t be split over frames). The real fix is a decision: on a phone, a section becomes its editor only when tapped.
